import time
then = int({query}) now = time.time() assuming_ms = False if (then > (now * 100)): then /= 1000 assuming_ms = True elapsed = now - then
then_str = time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', time.localtime(then))
assuming_ms_str = '' if assuming_ms: assuming_ms_str = ' (assuming input in ms)'
print """<?xml version="1.0"?><items> <item uid="desktop" arg="~/Desktop" valid="NO" type="file"> <title>Local time%s: %s</title> </item> <item> <title>Seconds elapsed: %s</title> </item> <item> <title>Minutes elapsed: %s</title> </item> <item> <title>Hours elapsed: %s</title> </item> <item> <title>Days elapsed: %s</title> </item> </items>""" % (assuming_ms_str, then_str, elapsed, elapsed / 60, elapsed/60/60, elapsed/60/60/24)
Enter in epoch time, in either seconds or milliseconds. It’ll show you what time that represents (in your local timezone), as well as how long ago that time was in various units.
